body: @josepharhar Should we add this to the agenda? It seems a useful addition?
Sure, I should probably try implementing this too. I wonder if we should make beforetoggle cancelable

We discussed this in our weekly triage meeting and we have a couple of questions:

 - Presumably these events will also fire on `appearance:auto`? If so are the concerns about beforetoggle being cancelable? I don't think this is a big concern as it's possible today, e.g. `data:text/html,<select onpointerdown="event.preventDefault()"><option>foo</option></select>`
 - On mobile UAs the popover is often modal. Will we run into issues here? The event should likely fire even with modal popovers; script still runs during this, so it shouldn't be problematic, but worth investigating further?
 - Is there a potential forward compat (or future backcompat) issue WRT `multiple`? If we only conditionally show a popover, and sometimes have an in-page control, does this mean JS that might otherwise expect a `beforetoggle` might _not_ get that toggle event, depending on the markup?

I think it's fine to make this only fire if the control is in appearance base but idk if that means you force a style calc on interaction which might not be ideal?

Conditionalising the firing should resolve the compat concerns regarding whether the select is a listbox or drop down?

> Presumably these events will also fire on appearance:auto? 

I figured yes, and imo there are no issues with it but if anything is blocking it then yeah only doing it for appearance:base is the main use case.

> * If so are the concerns about beforetoggle being cancelable? I don't think this is a big concern as it's possible today, e.g. `data:text/html,<select onpointerdown="event.preventDefault()"><option>foo</option></select>`

Yeah I agree, I don't see any issues with this. Perhaps only the opening beforetoggle should be cancelable but not the closing one?

 > On mobile UAs the popover is often modal. Will we run into issues here? The event should likely fire even with modal popovers; script still runs during this, so it shouldn't be problematic, but worth investigating further?

Yeah I could double check that script can still run while the picker is open in both appearance modes and perhaps write a test for that. Would that address this concern?

> Is there a potential forward compat (or future backcompat) issue WRT multiple? If we only conditionally show a popover, and sometimes have an in-page control, does this mean JS that might otherwise expect a beforetoggle might not get that toggle event, depending on the markup?

Yeah, it should depend on whether its a drop-down box or a listbox. We will soon have spec text which says that appearance:auto `<select multiple size=1>` might be one or the other depending on the platform, but I don't see why thats really an issue. If it is though, we could just fire these events for base appearance only.

Firing only for base appearance gets a little warty; I could do strange things like set `:hover{appearance:base}` or more practically: I might want to provide `appearance:auto` on certain platforms. It seems we're in agreement to fire for `appearance:auto` but I think we should be careful with events conditionally firing based on CSS, as that seems like it could lead to surprising variances.

From whatnot: in the case of `<select multiple size=1>` with `apperance:auto`, it will be a listbox in macos safari and a drop-down box everywhere else, which means that it will not fire the event on macos safari but will fire everywhere else. Some ways to address this:
- Let it not fire in this case. Maybe macos will support this picker in the future.
- Don't fire beforetoggle/toggle for `<select multiple size=1>`, even when it is rendered as a drop-down box.
- Don't fire beforetoggle/toggle for `appearance:auto`, since the drop-down box or listbox should be consistent in base appearance.

I think the question on how to feature detect this might play into things too. If we can't feature detect it we can't ever safely use it beyond enhancement (which I guess does solve the interop issues). Still could be issues when people make assumptions which eventually they definitely might...

Yeah, feature detection would be easier if showPicker didn't require user activation even in base appearance mode. You can feature detect support for toggle events for the dialog element synchronously and without user activation.

I think the fact it's already used on a multitude of elements means adding it on another one is fine? For select you know 99% that it's opened as a select based on tagname.

I also think using toggle and optionally beforetoggle is better than minting a new event name. Giving it a new name doesn't solve the questions raised above?

> I think the fact it's already used on a multitude of elements means adding it on another one is fine?

Imho it does not. I think the design decision that has been made, using it on a multitude of elements, was a mistake. Because it creates problems (that distinct events would not create).

> For select you know 99% that it's opened as a select based on tagname.

Call me a stickler for correctness but I really feel uneasy when I know that my code has gaps, even when they have a low probability of being hit one day. The prospect that I have to write code that is _probably_ correct _most of the time_ is not sitting right with me. Keep in mind: we are discussing a future feature here. Why not design it in a way that allows dependent code to reach 100% correctness? Let's not design it warty from the start.
Maybe I'm the only one struggling with the ambiguousness of the existing toggle event. I'm curious if others experienced the same issues.

> I also think using toggle and optionally beforetoggle is better than minting a new event name.

As I think minting a new event name would solve all previously discussed objections nicely, I obviously disagree here. But I don't know if there are strong arguments for keeping the pool of existing event names as it is and avoiding additions when possible.

> Giving it a new name doesn't solve the questions raised above?

Well I think it does. The questions raised above were mainly about how a select's toggle event needs to behave consistent to a popover's toggle event.
A newly minted distinct event name would not claim to be caused by a (top-layer) popover. It just signals "the select's picker opened/closed".

> By this logic, would it be better if instead of one change event, every type of element got its own prefixed change event? Like selectchange, textareachange, checkboxchange, radiochange, textchange, etc?

Good point. It made me question my earlier reasoning and I think I should clarify where exactly my struggle lies. It never gave me trouble that multiple element types can emit `change` events; if for example I should need to listen at the document root and handle all `change` events from `<input>` elements only, I can differentiate simply by `e.target.tagName === 'INPUT'` and rely on this check being sufficient.
But this isn't the case with the `toggle` events. (I actually do have a use case where I want to differentiate between _popover_ vs _modal dialog_ vs _other_ because they do have different effects. But independent from this I think web authors should be able to discern from a `toggle` event what exactly has happened.)
Currently the differentiation is difficult. Because `popover` is an attribute, a `<dialog>` or `<details>` can have the attribute. A toggle event originating in such an element is ambiguous.

> I can see how combining popover events with dialog events is confusing if you need to differentiate them, but I think that if we decided to fix this then it would be better to split popover events from element-specific ones, rather than make select have a different one and everything else use toggle/beforetoggle, or add flags to the toggle events to help differentiate.

Hits the nail on the head. I agree, it would solve the ambiguity if either "_popover events would be split from element-specific ones_" or "_flags would be added to the toggle events to help differentiate_". Then `toggle` events could well be used with `<select>` elements.

Should we raise a separate issue to discuss this further? Adding a flag to the event to say whuch 'type' it is seems maybe fine (though like you've mentioned we do have the necessary JS to detect already). Don't want this to get lost in the wider select toggle discussions.

I don't consider that a blocker though as the status quo already has this issue though?
